the Planck data favor a non-zero sum of neutrino masses, a positive lensing amplitude A (L) and dark energy with w < -1, while the CCCP cluster data prefer a lower matter power spectrum amplitude and a negative A(L).

the combined CMB and X- ray cluster data are consistent with LCDM cosmological model, but there are some tensions between the CMB data and the X-ray cluster data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the combined CMB and X-Ray cluster data can be used to put stringent constraints on neutrino masses, dark energy, and the CMB lensed power spectrum, and that the current tension between Planck and X-Ray cluster is not yet significant enough to rule out the vanilla LCDM model.
the combined CCCP X-ray data and the Planck data favor a cosmological model with a non-zero neutrinos, and a dark energy model with a negative equation of state.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of X-ray cluster data with CMB data and external data can help to break the degeneracies between cosmological parameters and thus to constrain cosmology in the non-vanilla cosmological models.

a non-zero neutrinos mass and A(L) >1 can be robustly confirmed by combining X-ray cluster data with the CMB data, while a constant w < -1 can be robust confirmed by combining XMM-Newton cluster data with the Planck data.
the joint CMB + X-ray cluster data can provide useful constraints on the neutrino mass in the non-vanilla cosmological models.
